t.1.46.1: When the embryo had been cut into seven parts, Diti, in deepest sorrow, spoke conciliatingly to Sahasrākṣa words hard to resist.
t.1.46.2: It is through my own fault that this embryo has been split into seven parts and rendered fruitless. There is no fault of yours in this, O lord of the gods, O slayer of Bala.
t.1.46.5: Let one roam the world of Brahmā, and likewise another the world of Indra; and let the third, of great renown, be known as Vāyu in the sky.
t.1.46.3: Now that my womb has met with this reversal, I wish a kindness to be done for me: let these seven become guardians of the stations of the seven Maruts.
t.1.46.4: Let these seven little sons of mine, divine in form, roam the sky as the Vātaskandhas, the regions of the winds, renowned by the name Mārutas.
t.1.46.7: Having heard those words of hers, the thousand-eyed Puraṃdara, the slayer of Bala, spoke these words to Diti with joined palms.
t.1.46.6: O best of gods, by your command four of my sons, having become gods, will roam through the directions, may good fortune be yours, and they will be renowned as the Mārutas by the very name you have given them.
t.1.46.8: All this shall come to pass just as you have said, there is no doubt. May good fortune be with you; your sons, having become gods, will roam about.
t.1.46.9: Having thus made their resolve in the grove of austerities, O Rāma, mother and son went to heaven with their purpose fulfilled. So we have heard.
t.1.46.11: O tiger among men, Ikṣvāku had a most righteous son, born of Alambuṣā, who was renowned by the name Viśāla.
t.1.46.10: This is that very region, O Kākutstha, once inhabited by mighty Indra, where he thus waited upon Diti, who had attained perfection through her austerity.
t.1.46.12: And by him, in this very place, a city named Viśālā was built.
t.1.46.13: O Rāma, the son of Viśāla was the mighty Hemacandra; after Hemacandra came the one renowned as Sucandra.
t.1.46.14: O Rāma, the son of Sucandra was renowned as Dhūmrāśva, and to Dhūmrāśva in turn was born a son, Sṛñjaya.
t.1.46.15: The son of Sṛñjaya was the glorious and valiant Sahadeva; the son of Sahadeva was Kuśāśva, supremely righteous.
t.1.46.16: Of Kuśāśva was born the greatly radiant and valorous Somadatta; and the son of Somadatta was renowned as Kākutstha.
t.1.46.17: His son, of great splendor, resembling an immortal and hard to conquer, named Sumati, now dwells in this very city.
t.1.46.18: By the grace of Ikṣvāku, all the kings of Vaiśālī were long-lived, great-souled, valorous and deeply righteous.
t.1.46.19: Here, today, O Rāma, we shall pass the night in comfort; tomorrow at daybreak, O best of men, you should see Janaka.
t.1.46.20: Sumati, of great splendour, foremost among the best of men and of great fame, hearing that Viśvāmitra had arrived, went forth to receive him.
t.1.46.21: Having offered supreme worship, together with his preceptor and his kinsmen, and having asked after his welfare with joined palms, he then spoke to Viśvāmitra.
t.1.46.22: I am blessed, I am favored, O sage, for you have come to my realm and granted me the sight of you; there is no one more fortunate than I.
